title: Backup Server Access — Compromised Images Detected

fields.organization: North Coast Regional Airport Authority — IT & Cybersecurity
fields.location: Main Server Room (Rack 4), Backup Storage Array
fields.summary: During a forensic audit of the backup server (SEC-SVR-02), I identified unauthorized access by the attacker’s service account (svc_update_04) 60 days ago. The account accessed the backup repository, copied data, and attempted to modify retention policies on two images. I cannot confirm whether the attacker planted a backdoor or corrupted the backup metadata. The most recent clean backup is 91 days old and only includes the file server. The AODB and Domain Controller were not backed up in that image. Any restore from a backup within the last 60 days risks reintroducing the malware.

findings.notes: Malicious service account (svc_update_04) accessed backup repository 60 days ago; attempted to alter retention policy on image #2026-0901

findings.item: File server backup image (91 days old)
findings.notes: Only image from before the 90-day compromise window; no evidence of tampering
Image was not fully verified; suspect of being compromised

findings.item: Domain Controller backup image (60 days old)
findings.notes: Image not verified; likely compromised
Retained 30-day window was modified to 7-day window by attacker; suggests data deletion intent
Logs show repeated access to backup repository; last access 47 days ago
Not included in any backup image from last 60 days
No evidence of compromise in backup
No access logs show abnormal behavior
No active beaconing from backup server

actionsTaken: Disabled backup replication to offsite storage
Notified IT Director and Ops IC via secure channel
Preserved original backup images and logs on write-protected media
recommendations: Do not restore any system from backup taken in last 60 days
Begin rebuild of all critical systems from gold images (2026-07-01) and patch via air-gapped workstations
Establish manual operations protocol for 72-hour window
Request CISA to validate recovery plan and provide forensic analysis support
fields.photosNote: 2 photos attached: IMG_20261022-004 (backup server access log), IMG_20261022-005 (service account activity timeline)

instructorNote: Critical decision point: Players must now decide whether to attempt recovery from potentially compromised backups. The attacker controls every credential and has had 90 days to embed persistence. This inject forces a choice between risk (restore) and cost (rebuild). Watch for hesitation to accept that 'clean' backups are not available.
